newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Feb 10.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government recalls change in Labour Law to explain why Monday is not a public holiday even though end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan fell on Sunday; says this is in line with Ivory Coast's development plans. In past, Monday following a national holiday on a Sunday was always a public holiday

- Head of Movement for Small and Medium-sized Companies (MPME) denounces civil service corruption and says government has not yet delivered on promises to promote private sector; tells World Bank, host of a consultative meeting, that it is allowing government to pull wool over its eyes.
- Committee reviewing Ivory Coast's cocoa sector reforms stresses need to ensure quality
- An airlink between Ivory Coast and Germany would depend on development of economic ties, German Ambassador Hans-Albrecht Schraepler says in interview

- Opposition Ivorian Popular Front (FPI) party urges dialogue to settle crisis in Ivory Coast's universities which has led to student strike and clashes between students and security forces; calls for release of detained students

- Issue of participation in broad-based government threatens to split the opposition Rally of the Republicans (RDR), a party former by defectors from the ruling Democratic Party (PDCI); youth wing heads opponents of participation
- Delegates to committee reviewing Ivory Coast's cocoa sector reforms complain of shortages of upcountry sacks for bagging beans
- Lack of proper town planning causes chaos as Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan expands; unlawful construction possible provided you know the right people, a Le Jour investigation shows.
